title: Founding, rebuilt: you choose the body, the world rolls the bloodline
question: You asked for more flexibility on body shape and movement. Three dials now: Q/E the body, A/D the lineage, Z/V how many. Is the body the right thing to have taken out of the roll — and is there a dial still missing?
context_md:
**The split is the change.** The first version rolled the body too, so you got three random animals. Now the body is a standing choice that applies to all three lineages on offer, and only the bloodline is rolled.

**The body choice is not cosmetic — it settles how the animal moves.** Six stocks: the common ant (two cells, dies whole), the hopper (the only shipped animal that actually jumps), the long ant (six cells, loses a tail and lives), the segmented ant (jointed, bends round corners), the broad ant (nine cells, digs a room), and pale chitin (plated from birth, twice an ant to bite through).

**Two of the six rolled traits are movement**: how fast it lives, and how tightly it turns. Both visible in this roll — LINE 1 turns tight, LINE 2 and 3 turn wide.

**Costs 170 / 209 / 144 against a pool of 600**, all affordable, so the choice is not made for you. Changing the body changes all three costs together, which is the dial doing something.

Still not built, and I would rather say so than have you find it: step 2 of the concept's own founding ritual — writing instincts as sentences. Rolling the brain is unsafe (a rolled genome gives you a colony that cannot forage and looks merely unlucky), but *writing* one is not, and the plain-speech genome readout that would have to become writable already exists.
